label: South-west Iberia
what: Neolithic cromlechs of the Alentejo (e.g. Almendres)
quote: The construction of these structures dates back to the 6th millennium BC. ... Almendres I 6000 BC (Early Neolithic), Almendres II 5000 BC (Middle Neolithic), and Almendres III 4000 BC (Late Neolithic). ... covers a period from the Neolithic to Chalcolithic.
note: End date: the source says the site's chronology runs into the Chalcolithic; I draw the faint tail to 3000 BC.

label: Britain and Ireland
what: Neolithic and Bronze Age stone circles
quote: These were constructed from 3200 to 2000 BCE in Great Britain, Ireland and Brittany. ... the stone circle tradition existed between 3300 and 900 BCE. Around 1,300 of them are recorded.
source: Wikipedia, Stone circles in the British Isles and Brittany (citing Burl)

label: Brittany
what: Neolithic circles and horseshoes (e.g. Er Lannic, Kergonan)
quote: These were constructed from 3200 to 2000 BCE in Great Britain, Ireland and Brittany.
source: Wikipedia, Stone circles in the British Isles and Brittany
note: Same source and range as Britain and Ireland.

label: Pyrenees
what: Cromlechs or baratzak: small rings around cremation burials
quote: The radiocarbon dates place them in the Late Bronze Age (Ondarre). ... most fall in the first half of the first millennium BC. ... Late Bronze Age (c. 1200 BC); they continued to be built during the Iron Age (first millennium BC).
source: Mujika-Alustiza et al. 2018, Munibe Antropologia-Arkeologia 69; and Harrespil (Hispanopedia)
note: Second source: https://es.hispanopedia.com/wiki/Harrespil (my translation of the Spanish).

label: Ship settings
what: Stone ships of Scandinavia and the Baltic
quote: The ships vary in size and were erected from c. 1000 BCE to 1000 CE ... usually from the latter part of the Nordic Bronze Age, c. 1000 BCE to 500 BCE

label: Scandinavia and Finland
quote: The stone circles of the Iron Age (c. 500 BC to c. 400 AD) ... were a characteristic burial custom of southern Scandinavia and Southwestern Finland, especially on Gotland and in Gotaland.

label: Pomerania
what: Gothic (Wielbark culture) stone circles, e.g. Odry, Wesiory, Grzybnica
quote: Appearing in the later 1st century, this type is found between the Vistula and the Kashubian and Krajenskian lakelands (Odry and Wesiory sites) ... reaching into the Koszalin region (Grzybnica site). [Wielbark culture] ca. 100 to 400.
note: Start: later 1st century AD (I use AD 75). End: the end of the Wielbark culture, ca. 400. Core AD 75 to 200 from medievalheritage.eu: Odry 'settled here around 70/80 AD ... around 200, they left Pomerania' (https://medievalheritage.eu/en/main-page/heritage/poland/odry-prehistoric-cemetery/); Grzybnica 'around 80-120 AD ... ended around 160-200 AD' (https://medievalheritage.eu/en/main-page/heritage/poland/grzybnica-prehistoric-cemetery/).
